notes:
T426 (spec: assertion ledger and status utility) — SPEC ONLY, no implementation. Delivers docs/infra/assertion-ledger/spec.md: a 12-section specification for an append-only assertion ledger and the derived-status display utility it enables.

EVALUATION OF T425/argus RELATIONSHIP (§7): argus --mode doctor IS the display utility the operator described. It already groups findings by NEEDS ACTION / CAN CLOSE / WATCH / CLEAN, already names evidence and fix commands, and already says CAN CLOSE when a row is done and clean. The assertion ledger gives it a better substrate — instead of inferring console state from command output (git, managent, claimlint, ps), it reads assertions directly and cross-checks against the observable world. No new tool, no new output format.

KEY DESIGN DECISIONS:
- The assertion record (§2): actor (seat identifier), verb (controlled vocabulary of 16 verbs), object, timestamp, basis (performed/observed/reported-by — the field that separates aspiration from actuality), supersedes (for corrections), meta (verb-specific detail).
- Append-only (§3): assertions are never mutated or deleted. Corrections are new assertions superseding earlier ones; both remain readable — the same principle managent amend already uses for verdicts, generalised.
- Status is DERIVED, never stored (§4): the doctor computes console state from the assertion log + cross-check against observable world. Disagreements are surfaced, not resolved.
- Console lifecycle (§5): dispatched → working → reported → absorbed → recommended-for-close → closed. Distinct from row lifecycle. absorbed and recommended-close are Orchestrator-only assertions — that is where the operator-requested accountability lands.
- Anti-skip property (§6): every step is either REFUSED (mechanically gated — claim, done, git-commit-mine) or VISIBLE-GAP (reported by doctor — missing absorbed, missing recommended-close, missing closed). No step is neither.
- Mistake patterns as data (§8): pattern observations are assertions in the same log (meta.pattern), not a separate register. Minimal queryable shape: pattern ID, description, occurrences, latest instances, detection method, remediation status.
- Migration cost (§9): managent appends assertions on existing verbs (~200 lines Zig); argus doctor reads assertion log (~300 lines Python); git-commit-mine appends refused (~20 lines bash). Total ~640 lines, medium risk. tasks.json is untouched — the assertion log is additive, not a replacement. The two-sources-of-truth problem is resolved by the doctor reporting disagreements rather than resolving them.
- Explicit non-scope (§10): no separate CLI tool, no tasks.json replacement, no stored derived state, no prose generation, no looping console, no real-time push, no assertion log for argus sweep/checklist, no tasks.json schema migration.
- Minimal subset recommendation (§11): Phase 1 (ship first) — assertion record format + managent append on existing verbs + doctor console-lifecycle-gap check + git-commit-mine refused assertion. Phase 2 (separate row) — console as first-class entity + mistake patterns + doctor derives all status from assertion log.

BARS MET:
- Specification only, no implementation, no schema migration, no managent code.
- Migration costed honestly: what changes, what does not, what could go wrong, effort estimate.
- Smallest thing that closes the operator's actual pain: the doctor's CAN CLOSE line becomes checkable rather than inferred. The operator reads one line, finds the backing assertions, closes the console.
- Names what NOT to build: seven explicit exclusions in §10.
- argus --mode doctor IS the utility (§7.1), per the operator's own guess — evaluated honestly, not a parallel tool.
- Anti-skip: every step enumerated and classified in §6.
- Mistake patterns: minimal queryable shape in §8, using the assertion log rather than a separate register.
- Acceptance criteria enumerated in §12.

LANDMARK: advances L1 (the dashboard tells the truth) and L4 (the ledger is clean) — gives argus --mode doctor a structured substrate so it reports what happened rather than inferring it, and makes the operator's most-asked question ("can I close this console?") answerable without asking the Orchestrator.
